overall: The AG found the Council violated the Open Meeting Law because a remote councilor was not clearly audible at times; it declined to review the claim that he was not allowed to make a motion.

allegations.summary: Councilor was not allowed to bring a motion to refer a zoning matter to the Ways and Means committee at the August 2 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the allegation that Councilor O’Brien was not allowed to bring a motion, even if true, would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law we decline to review the allegation.

allegations.summary: A councilor participating remotely by phone was inaudible at times during the August 2 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: However, there were times during the meeting when Councilor O’Brien was not clearly audible.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Council’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
